trajectory_summary: This is a short, low-friction call that moves from a cost question straight through the qualifier checklist to a booked appointment with almost no resistance. The rep ran the verify sequence efficiently but let two significant items slide past unused: an unqualified 'free installation' promise made in the first 20 seconds, and a disavowed $1,000 bill the customer explicitly said wasn't real. The call ends booked, but with loose threads a closer needs flagged.

observed_outcome.quote: Wednesday at nine. Okay. And you said it was the Yes, sir.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Wednesday the 22nd) and time (9AM) are both confirmed and restated by the rep, meeting the bar for a booked appointment; no co-owner was identified since the customer stated she is the only one on title.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: The first bill they sent me was, like, a thousand and something dollars dollars.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The customer herself disavowed this number as not a real bill ('so we know that wasn't a real bill'), so the rep correctly did not build urgency on it — but no flip was attempted, and the pending corrected bill was never set up as a concrete follow-up item to anchor on later.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: Do you have a utility bill with you, or do you get them online?
bill_document_audit.result_quote: No. And I don't. The thing is because I just moved here,
bill_document_audit.reasoning: Customer has no valid bill to provide because the utility is still correcting a bypassed-meter billing error; rep pivoted to square footage instead of setting a concrete plan to collect the corrected bill later.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked what interested the customer in solar; the customer's opening question about free installation is cost-curiosity but was never developed into a stated motivation.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: Yeah. Yeah. This is a solar program they're offering that offers free installation.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This is the single most consequential line on the call — an unconditional 'free installation' claim delivered before any qualifying happened, creating a promise the closer must now manage or walk back in the proposal.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. This is a solar program they're offering that offers free installation.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep answers a cost/program-mechanics question definitively and without qualification before any verify items are run. 'Free installation' is a claim about program financing that belongs to the closer's proposal conversation, not an unqualified opener line.

key_moments.quote: Behind the home. The trees that were around the home, I got them cut down.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer proactively discloses she already removed trees that were shading the home — a concrete, unprompted improvement to solar viability that increases lead quality.

key_moments.quote: so they had to guesstimate me a bill. So they guesstimated me. It was a really high bill that they guesstimated. So I actually haven't even received my first my first bill yet.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a live, emotionally-charged billing complaint (a guessed bill she considers inflated) tied to a utility she's clearly annoyed with. This is exactly the kind of alignment-against-the-utility material objection_inversion is built for, but the rep does not flip it into urgency or savings framing.

key_moments.quote: Okay. And who's the utility company?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep captures the utility name (Pepco) correctly per script, but the surrounding billing chaos (bypassed meter, incorrect readings, pending corrected bill) is a live open item that never gets a clear next step — no request for the corrected bill once received, no text/email follow-up instruction tied to it.
